# dbt_marketing/models/staging/stg_touchpoints.sql (42 lines)
-- One row per marketing touch, cleaned and typed. No business logic.
--
-- Staging's job is to make the source safe to build on: stable column names,
-- explicit types, trimmed strings. Anything that involves a decision about
-- meaning (what counts as a session, which touch gets credit) belongs
-- downstream. Keeping that line sharp is what makes it possible to say
-- "the source is fine, the logic is wrong" when a number looks off.

with source as (

    select * from {{ source('raw', 'touchpoints') }}

),

renamed as (

    select
        -- Composite key. The generator has no touch-level id, so we build one
        -- from the natural key; the tests below assert it is actually unique.
        cast(user_id as varchar) || '-' || cast(touch_number as varchar)
            as touchpoint_id,

        cast(user_id as bigint)          as user_id,

        -- Left 0-based here on purpose: renaming is staging's job, re-indexing
        -- is not. int_touchpoints_sessionized derives a 1-based touch_seq.
        cast(touch_number as integer)    as touch_index,

        -- raw arrives as TIMESTAMP_NS from pandas. Nothing here needs
        -- nanoseconds, and the wider type propagates awkwardly into joins.
        cast(touched_at as timestamp)    as touched_at,

        lower(trim(channel))             as channel,
        lower(trim(campaign))            as campaign,

        cast(cost as double)             as touch_cost_usd

    from source

)

select * from renamed
